findings.description: A committed case exercises a blocked state on a clean tree and asserts the refusal, and it discriminates: relocating the guard below the clean-tree exit turns it red while the four dirty cases stay green.
findings.evidence:
CLAUSE SATISFIED, both halves.

HALF 1 -- the committed case (tests/sync.bats:183-200), read line by line:
  :184 fresh_repo                      -> builds its own repo, nothing written after
  :185 git checkout -q --detach HEAD   -> blocked state, no file written
  :187-188 porcelain="$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain)"; [ -z "$porcelain" ]
                                       -> pre-run porcelain asserted EMPTY
  :192 run bash "$SCRIPT"              -> reaches the real script with a clean tree
  :194 [ "$status" -ne 0 ]             -> refusal
  :195 assert_contains "$DETACHED_MSG"          -> names its state
  :196-197 assert_not_contains "$REBASE_MSG" / "$MERGE_MSG"  -> other two families absent
  :198 assert_not_contains "Nothing to commit. Already in sync."  -> the fall-through discriminator
  :199 rev-list --count HEAD equals before_count captured at :190 -> no commit created
The needle at :198 is checked against $output, which is the same merged stream :26
(`exec > >(tee -a "$LOG") 2>&1`) writes to $HOME/.local/state/dotfiles/last-sync.log,
with $HOME redirected to $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/home at :32. Asserting the log and asserting
$output are the same assertion here.
Nothing is written into the scratch repo between fresh_repo and the run: the only files
under $REPO are seed.txt from setup, and the :188 assertion is what proves it at run time.

HALF 2 -- RELOCATION MUTATION (a move, not a deletion).
Digest bracket BEFORE:
  $ shasum -a 256 dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync
  c90191bfb7fa6d48dc7deb5d6bb51fe41cebfa84446816ab206a2410fc04dc73
Backup taken to an absolute path OUTSIDE the repo before any mutation
(<scratch>/sync.orig, same digest). git commit / git reset / git checkout were never
used on this file; the mutant went in with cp and came out with cp.
Mutation: script lines 130-151 (the guard comment + the if/elif/elif block) moved to sit
BELOW the clean-tree early exit, which is at :153-156 in the working tree (:130-133 at the
298c8a6 baseline the clause cites). Verified a pure relocation, not an edit:
  $ diff <(sort sync.orig) <(sort sync.mutant)   -> identical multiset of lines
  $ bash -n sync.mutant                          -> OK (parses; nothing flipped on syntax)
Mutant in place, digest 7865833e4cc311e2e2dbaa22d9a5f6321421876616b69ce0b1ee70355a93e21d:
  $ bats tests/sync.bats
  1..5
  ok 1 sync: attached branch with no operation in progress commits normally
  ok 2 sync: detached HEAD refuses, names itself, and leaves the repo untouched
  ok 3 sync: rebase in progress refuses, names itself, and leaves the repo untouched
  ok 4 sync: merge in progress refuses, names itself, and leaves the repo untouched
  not ok 5 sync: detached HEAD refuses on a clean tree, before the clean-tree exit ever runs
  # (in test file tests/sync.bats, line 194)
  #   `[ "$status" -ne 0 ]' failed
Exactly the required discrimination: the new clean case goes red on the forbidden
placement while all four dirty cases stay green. This is the placement regression none of
T-001's three per-detector deletions can catch, since every detector is still present and
still reachable on the dirty path.
Restored with cp and verified:
  $ diff <scratch>/sync.orig dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync   -> no output
Digest bracket AFTER:
  c90191bfb7fa6d48dc7deb5d6bb51fe41cebfa84446816ab206a2410fc04dc73   (matches)

SUITE, post-restore:
  $ bats --count tests/          -> 125          (above the required 124)
  $ bats tests/                  -> exit 0; 125 'ok', 0 'not ok'
  $ bats tests/lint.bats         -> exit 0; ok 1 no bare [[ or (( on the guarded surface
  $ bats tests/sync.bats         -> 5/5 ok
  $ git rev-parse HEAD           -> 298c8a69f839b336c248ec1b1b6607b4f43de589 (unchanged)

NO PRE-EXISTING CASE TOUCHED, cross-checked two independent ways:
  $ git diff 298c8a6 -- tests/ | grep -c '^-[^-]'   -> 0
  (that command is vacuous on its own here, since tests/sync.bats is untracked, so:)
  1. The LaunchAgent's incidental capture 75a2325 holds a 181-line tests/sync.bats
     committed at 22:00:12, before the 22:06:13 mtime of the current 200-line file.
     `diff -u 75a2325:tests/sync.bats tests/sync.bats` is one hunk, @@ -179,3 +179,22 @@,
     19 added lines and 0 removed -- the harness at :1-118 and all four T-002 cases are
     byte-identical.
  2. Every line number the T-002 checker's own verdict cites still lands on the same
     content: :25 SCRIPT, :27-29 the message constants, :107-118 fresh_repo, the four
     @test headers at :120/:132/:148/:164, the marker builds at :134/:150/:169, the
     invocations at :124/:139/:155/:174, and the assertion blocks at :126-129/:141-145/
     :157-161/:176-180.

findings.description: The new case drives the real dotfiles-sync against its own freshly built throwaway repo, reimplements none of the guard's logic, and has no path to the real source dir if a stub fails.
findings.evidence:
CLAUSE SATISFIED. Both rubric questions answered from the file, then corroborated
by behavior.

Q1 -- does the new case invoke the real script, or assert against a copy of the guard's
logic? It invokes the real script. tests/sync.bats:192 is `run bash "$SCRIPT"`, with
SCRIPT="$SRC/dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync" at :25 and SRC="${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/.."
at :24. Grepping the new case's own 18 lines (:183-200) for guard predicates --
symbolic-ref, rebase-merge, rebase-apply, MERGE_HEAD -- returns nothing: there is no
reimplementation to assert against. The only guard strings it touches are the shared
constants DETACHED_MSG / REBASE_MSG / MERGE_MSG at :27-29, used as assert_contains and
assert_not_contains needles, never as logic. Corroborated behaviorally rather than taken
on the read: under the B-5 relocation mutation this case flipped to `not ok`, which is
impossible for a case asserting against a copy of the logic, since the copy did not move.

Q2 -- its own fresh scratch repo, or another case's? Its own. :184 calls fresh_repo, which
at :107-118 does `git init -q --bare "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/origin.git"` and
`git init -q "$REPO"` with REPO="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/repo", then seeds, commits, and pushes.
No reset, no clean, no reuse. I confirmed BATS_TEST_TMPDIR is genuinely per-@test on this
bats (1.14.0) rather than assuming it, with a throwaway probe outside the repo:
  A=/var/folders/.../bats-run-DFFLbq/test/1
  B=/var/folders/.../bats-run-DFFLbq/test/2
  ISOLATED        (a directory made in test A is absent in test B)
So the detached HEAD, the empty porcelain at :188 and the commit count at :190 all belong
to this case alone.

Reachability of the real ~/.local/share/chezmoi, B-2's second half: the script derives
SRC from `chezmoi source-path` at :18 under `set -euo pipefail` (:16). The harness exports
an authoritative PATH at :48, `export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"` -- replaced, not
prepended -- and the real binary lives only at /opt/homebrew/bin/chezmoi (`which -a
chezmoi`; /usr/bin/chezmoi and /bin/chezmoi do not exist). A stub that failed to take
effect therefore leaves `chezmoi` unresolvable and the run aborts at :18; there is no
fallback path on which SRC could become the real source dir. $STUBS ($BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/
stubs) and the redirected $HOME ($BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/home) are siblings of $REPO, not nested
inside it, so neither leaves an untracked entry in the porcelain the case asserts empty.
